Title: b'Updating deepchem to follow 4 spaces for indentation'
Body:
b'Context: DeepChem codebase currently uses 2 spaces for indents.
Proposal: Migrate to 4 spaces for indents.

Here is a breakdown of PRs to update indentation.

- [x] The first pull request should update setup.cfg to use indent_width as 4 for yapf.

Updating core modules style are:

- [x] Update deepchem/data/datasets.py (Loc: 3102)
- [x] Update deepchem/data rest of the modules (Loc: 2168)
- [x] Update deepchem/feat/base_classes.py, graph_features.py (LoC: 1567)
- [x] Update optimizers.py, losses.py, models.py, callbacks.py, init.py in deepchem/models dir (LoC: 1677)
- [x] Update deepchem.models.torch_models.layers.py, torch_model.py (LoC: 3887)-
- [ ] Update deepchem.models.keras_model.py, graph_models.py (LoC: 2544)

Updating deepchem/feat directory:

- [ ] deepchem/feat/molecule_featurizers and all files (LoC: 3721)
- [ ] deepchem/feat/complex_featurizers and all files (LoC: 1994)
- [ ] deepchem/feat/tests all files (LoC: 3312)
- [ ] rest of all .py deepchem/feat directory (LoC: 1644)

Updating deepchem molnet directory:

- [ ] all .py files in deepchem/molnet directory (LoC: 2374)
- [ ] all .py files in deepchem/molnet/load_function dir, load_dataset_template.py, molnet.py (LoC: 432)
- [ ] rest of all .py files in deepchem/molnet/load_function dir (LoC: 4261)
- [ ] all .py files in deepchem/molnet/material_datasets (LoC: 538)

Updating deepchem models directory:

- [ ] Update deepchem/models/layers.py (LoC: 3858)
- [ ] Update gan.py, seqtoseq.py, chemnet_layers.py, wandblogger.py, chemnet_models.py in deepchem/models dir (LoC: 2121)
- [ ] Update rest of the files in deepchem/models dir
- [ ] Update dmpnn.py, kfac_optimizer.py, ferminet.py, cgcnn.py, gcn.py (LoC: 2125)
- [ ] Update gat.py, pagtn.py, mat.py, normalizing_flows_pytorch.py, cnn.py, megnet.py, mpnn.py, lcnn.py, attentivefp.py (2803)
- [ ] Update test_reload.py, test_overfit.py, test_layers.py, test_layers_from_config.py, test_torch_model.py test_keras_model.py, test_losses.py in deepchem/models/tests dir (LoC: 4975)
- [ ] rest of the tests in deepchem/models/tests dir (loc: 5129)

Utils directory:

- [ ] rdkit_utils.py, data_utils.py, molecule_feature_utils.py in deepchem/utils directory (LoC: 2657)
- [ ] evaluate.py noncovalent_utils.py fragment_utils.py coordinate_box_utils.py pdbqt_utils.py in deepchem/utild dir (LoC: 2094)
- [ ] save.py pytorch_utils.py typing.py vina_utils.py debug_utils.py init.py hash_utils.py genomics_utils.py fake_data_generator.py sequence_utils.py voxel_utils.py geometry_utils.py electron_sampler.py conformers.py docking_utils.py in deepchem/utils dir (LoC: 2193)
- [ ] all files in deepchem/utils/test dir (loc: 1892)

Other files and directories:

- [ ] deepchem/dock and subdirectories (LoC: 1468)
- [ ] deepchem/splits and subdirectories (LoC: 2462)
- [ ] deepchem/rl directory and subdirectories: LoC 2153
- [ ] deepchem/trans directory: Loc 2786
- [x] deepchem/trans/tests directory: Loc 1302
- [x] deepchem/hyper directory: Loc 1735
- [ ] deepchem/metalearning and subdirectories (LoC: 433)
- [ ] deepchem/metrics directory and subdirectories: LoC 1560
- [x] Update deepchem/data tests (Loc: 3018)

**Other notes**
When a contributor updates a file and if the file is following 2 spaces for tab, a first PR should be made to update style and a subsequent PR should contain the contribution. This will help in easier code reviews.

Title: b'gusty1g'
Body:
b'When parsing the SMILES string, I got `SMILES Parse Error: syntax error while parsing: CC@@Hc1ccccc1C(F)(F)F`. This error is generated from rdkit which is used by deepchem. When the featurizer gets an error during featurization of a datapoint, it appends an empty array. And when a dataset with empty array was passed to the model, it raised IndexError at somepoint where the architecture expected to get a valid index but got a None value.

To fix this, I would suggest to use `CSVLoader` which drops data points where featurization has failed during creation of dataset. Here is an example which I used for the above case:
```
featurizer = dc.feat.DMPNNFeaturizer(features_generators=['rdkit_desc_normalized'])
loader = dc.data.CSVLoader(["y"], feature_field="smiles", featurizer=featurizer)
dataset = loader.create_dataset('smiles.csv')
```

Also, the model should be initialized as 
```
model = DMPNNModel(mode = 'classification', n_classes=2, n_tasks= 1, global_features_size=200, model_dir='...')
```
because we are using an additional feature generator here which generates feature of size 200. This should be passed as an argument to the model in `global_features_size`.

I will label this as docs since we have to improve our docs that we should pass `global_features_size` when `features_generator` is used during featurization.'

Title: b'NormalizationTransformer.untransform edge case for batch_size = 1'
Body:
b'Thanks to a bug-report on gitter, we have this interesting failing test case:

```
  def test_normalization_batch_one(self):                              
    """This test is based on a user bug report.
          
    When `batch_size==1` and `n_tasks > 1`,
    `NormalizationTransformer.untransform` had a weird edge case where 
    it would return a larger output that input.
    """ 
    n_samples = 11                                                     
    n_features = 5 
    n_tasks = 2                                                        
    train_dataset = dc.data.NumpyDataset(np.random.rand(n_samples, n_features), np.random.rand(n_samples, n_tasks))                            
    
    transformer = dc.trans.NormalizationTransformer(                   
            transform_y=True, dataset=train_dataset, move_mean=True)   
    
    # batch of size 1 shape                                            
    batch = np.random.rand(1, 2, 1)                                    
    output = transformer.untransform(batch)                            
      
    assert len(batch) == len(output)
```

This currently fails because of this batch of code in `NormalizationTransformer.untransform` (https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/deepchem/trans/transformers.py#L200):

```
for dim in z_shape:
  if dim != n_tasks and dim == 1:
    y_min = np.expand_dims(y_min, -1)
    y_max = np.expand_dims(y_max, -1)
```

The edge case occurs when `batch_size==1` and it erroneously expands the batch dimension outwards. This can be fixed by preventing expansion from happening on the batch dimension with an explicit guard:

```
# Get the reversed shape of z: (..., n_tasks, batch_size)        
z_shape.reverse()
# Find the task dimension of z
for ind, dim in enumerate(z_shape):
  if ind < (len(z_shape) - 1) and dim == 1:
    # Prevent broadcasting on wrong dimension                    
    y_stds = np.expand_dims(y_stds, -1)
    y_means = np.expand_dims(y_means, -1)
```

I've made this fix in #1792 and will upstream it in a later PR'

Title: b'Feature to store and load model configurations'
Body:
b'A deep learning model have number of config options, like dropout, hidden layer size for each of the hidden layer, activation, number of attention heads, type of readout in graph models etc.

It will be nice to have an utility to save a model config to a file which can be used to initialize a model later, like for evaluation.
Some ideas:
- For every model, a config object (a simple python dictionary) which contains the model configuration parameters and methods to save the config to a file, as a json or yaml can be created.

One advantage is that it will reduce the number of arguments in the call to initialize the model, making the model initialization call cleaner.'

Title: b'lilleswing'
Body:
b'we do -- it is a legacy thing we should get rid of

@akourm910e you can always make the dataset yourself.

```python
from rdkit import Chem
import numpy as np
import deepchem as dc


def load_sdf(fname, tasks=list(), featurizer=None):
  """
  Parameters
  ----------
  fname: str
    filename of sdf to load
  tasks: list of str
    tasks from the sdf file to load
  Returns
  -------
  """
  suppl = Chem.SDMolSupplier(fname)
  mols = [x for x in suppl]
  if featurizer is None:
    X = np.array(mols)
  else:
    X = featurizer.featurize(mols)
  if len(tasks) == 0:
    y = np.zeros((len(mols), 1))
    return dc.data.NumpyDataset(X, y)

  y = np.zeros((len(mols), len(tasks)))
  w = np.zeros((len(mols), len(tasks)))
  for i, mol in enumerate(mols):
    for j, task in enumerate(tasks):
      try:
        y[i][j] = float(mol.GetProp(task))
        w[i][j] = 1
      except:
        w[i][j] = 0

  return dc.data.NumpyDataset(X, y, w)


if __name__ == "__main__":
  ds = load_sdf("datasets/membrane_permeability.sdf",
                ["LogP(RRCK)"],
                featurizer=dc.feat.ConvMolFeaturizer())
  model = dc.models.GraphConvModel(1,mode='regression')
  model.fit(ds)
  model.predict(ds)
```'

try:

Title: b'Depreciate MATEmbedding layer'
Body:
b'MATEmbedding layer is used to generate an embedding of output node features in `torch_models.mat.MAT`  model. The layer wraps `nn.Linear` and `nn.Dropout` layers. It does not add any other functionality. To replace it, we can directly add a Linear and Dropout and linear layer in `torch_models.mat.MAT` where it is being used. 
I would like to suggest depreciating it for two reasons:
- with less number of choices, users will be able to decide better on what layers to use.
- lesser lines of code, easier to maintain

Before depreciating, we should consider how depreciating it will affect reloading of existing models MAT (Molecular Attention Transformer) models.'

Title: b'Loading of top layer in pretrained model when bias is False'
Body:
b"When we are reloading model weights with `include_top=False` using `load_from_pretrained` method, if the top layer has bias set as False, weights for the below the top layer is not getting copied. Here is the code to reproduce:
```
import deepchem as dc

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):    
    def __init__(self):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.dense = nn.Linear(in_features=8, out_features=2, bias=True)
        self.head = nn.Linear(in_features=2, out_features=1, bias=False)
        
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.head(self.dense(x)) 

pre = Model()
pre_dc = dc.models.TorchModel(pre, loss=dc.models.losses.L2Loss())
pre_dc.save_checkpoint()

fine = Model()
fine_dc = dc.models.TorchModel(fine, loss=dc.models.losses.L2Loss())

fine_dc.load_from_pretrained(pre_dc, include_top=False)

print (fine_dc.model.state_dict())
OrderedDict([('dense.weight',
              tensor([[-0.1105, -0.3411, -0.0083, -0.0793,  0.1559,  0.2183,  0.2238, -0.2569],
                      [ 0.2783, -0.2978,  0.0273, -0.0058, -0.2408, -0.1351,  0.0046, -0.3154]])),
             ('dense.bias', tensor([-0.0330, -0.0030])),
             ('head.weight', tensor([[-0.4924, -0.0605]]))])

print (pre_dc.model.state_dict())
OrderedDict([('dense.weight',
              tensor([[-0.1105, -0.3411, -0.0083, -0.0793,  0.1559,  0.2183,  0.2238, -0.2569],
                      [ 0.2783, -0.2978,  0.0273, -0.0058, -0.2408, -0.1351,  0.0046, -0.3154]])),
             ('dense.bias', tensor([-0.1272, -0.2554])),
             ('head.weight', tensor([[0.4836, 0.2152]]))])
```

Expected output: For the layer `dense.bias`, pre_dc model and fine_dc should have same weights. In source, 

https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/8f5267cdec58449dcd5972c3d531447d0c0900ff/deepchem/models/torch_models/torch_model.py#L1078-L1080

the above lines cause skipping of an additional layer when bias is False.

Some ideas:
- I think we should have an option to specify whether top layer has bias or not.
- Another option is to update our `load_from_pretrained` method to use model.state_dict() and match keys with an assignment map indicating layer names to load. Currently, assignment map is a dictionary of tensors with keys as tensors in source model, values as tensors in destination model (finetune model). The user has to specify assignment map. If the assignment map uses state_dict, users can avoid specifying top layers in the state_dict.
"

b'##  Bug

If a model is trained with a GPU but it's trying to reload the model when GPU isn't available (for example on a different machine), torch.load() fails unless the device is explicitly specified as 'cpu'.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Train torch model on GPU
2. Transfer model to non-GPU computer
3. Try to load the model with torch_model.restore()

<!-- If you have a code sample, error messages, stack traces, please provide it here as well. -->
[torch_restore_stack_trace.txt](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/files/8943790/torch_restore_stack_trace.txt)


## Expected behavior
Even if GPU isn't available, the model should be able to load on a different machine. 
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->

## Environment

* OS: Red Hat Enterprise Linux Server release 7.9 (Maipo)
* Python version: 3.7.10
* DeepChem version: 2.6.1
* RDKit version (optional): 2022.03.01
* TensorFlow version (optional): 2.8.0

  def restore(self,
              checkpoint: Optional[str] = None,
              model_dir: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    """Reload the values of all variables from a checkpoint file.

    Parameters

      checkpoint will be chosen automatically.  Call get_checkpoints() to get a
      list of all available checkpoints.
    model_dir: str, default None
      Directory to restore checkpoint from. If None, use self.model_dir.  If
      checkpoint is not None, this is ignored.
    """
    self._ensure_built()

    ###

    ###

    if checkpoint is None:
      checkpoints = sorted(self.get_checkpoints(model_dir))

      checkpoint = checkpoints[0]

    ###
    data = torch.load(checkpoint, map_location=device)
    ###

    self.model.load_state_dict(data['model_state_dict'])
    self._pytorch_optimizer.load_state_dict(data['optimizer_state_dict'])
    self._global_step = data['global_step']
```'

Title: b'Document using Scikit-learn models for multilabel datasets with missing labels'
Body:
b'##  Feature

Currently it is unclear how multilabel datasets are treated for Scikit-learn estimators, many of which are used in MoleculeNet. For neural networks, this is trivial, as we can use masked loss or weights matrix, but for Scikit-learn compatibility, there must be no missing values. How this is handled is currently not documented at all.

As far as I understand, going through [this example using Random Forest](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/examples/pcba/pcba_sklearn.py):
1. No multitask models are actually used, just as many single task models as there are tasks. This includes models that can handle multilabel classification, like Random Forest, but we cannot use them that way, since they cannot handle NaN in targets.
2. Dataset is splitted into multiple copies, one per task. Missing values are removed from each task, creating clean single task classification datasets.
3. We fit as many models as there are tasks, and then during prediction for new samples (e.g. on validation / test set) we use each model to predict its task, and concatenate the predictions.
4. For calculating metrics, we simply average metric value calculated separately for each task.
5. The same set of hyperparameters is used in all models created this way. This also means that during hyperparameter optimization we will select hyperparams such that we perform the best on average across all tasks (due to how metrics are handled).

If this is correct, this could be added to the documentation, or at least as a tutorial in examples.

## Motivation

This is important to understand how Scikit-learn models are trained and on which data.'

Title: b'gusty1g'
Body: b'Yes, you are right. We should document it.'

Title: b'rbharath'
Body: b'These errors are a function of the underlying dataset. QM7/8/9 exhaustively list small molecules with 7/8/9 heavy atoms, which can trigger RDKit warnings about structural stability.'

Title: b'j-adamczyk'
Body: b'@rbharath ok, but if this is an expected behavior, then DeepChem should filter out those warnings. As I understand, they are at the C++ level, not Python level, but can still be controlled through RDKit Python library, see [this issue](https://github.com/rdkit/rdkit/issues/2683). Turning this off will also result in performance improvement, as the number of output warnings is huge and this amount of I/O definitely slows down computing. Turning this off can be added e.g. as `ignore_warnings` and `ignore_errors` options. If they have default `True` value for QM7/8/9 datasets, this will suppress warnings and also be backwards-compatible. What do you think?'

Title: b'Get rid of yapf'
Body:
b"Can we switch to some other formatter instead of yapf?  I really really dislike it.  To begin with, it produces horrible looking code.  Here's an example from a file I just checked in.  I wrote a simple, readable line of code:

```Python
advantages[j-1] += self.a3c.discount_factor * self.a3c.advantage_lambda * advantages[j]
```

But here is how yapf decided to reformat that:

```Python
advantages[
    j -
    1] += self.a3c.discount_factor * self.a3c.advantage_lambda * advantages[
        j]
```

Seriously???  That looks like something someone would write as a joke.

I could live with that if it weren't for a bigger problem: it doesn't produce consistent results.  Although I'm running exactly the same version of yapf on my computer as what's on travis, it still sometimes produces different results.  Every @#$% time I make a change to layers.py and run yapf, I then have to go in and manually fix a few lines that yapf has changed, but that will cause travis to fail if I don't put them back again."

Title: b'DeepChem Model Wishlist'

Implementations of any of these models would be a great contribution to DeepChem. As an incentive for contributors, contributing a model would earn authorship on one of our upcoming manuscripts! If you have bandwidth to contribute an implementation, please chime in below 

- [ ] IterRefLSTMs from https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acscentsci.6b00367 (We have some old DeepChem code that doesn't work in today's DeepChem that can be ported, see https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/issues/2070).

Title: b'Dropout layers are not activated when predicting uncertainty in some models'
Body:
b'##  Bug

Dropout layers are not activated when `predict_uncertainty` is called in some models, so the epistemic component of the uncertainty is not calculated.  I think the models based on KerasModel and TorchModel which support uncertainty prediction are affected, e.g. GraphConv, DAG.

When the model is called in `_predict` during the loop over dropout masks in `predict_uncertainty`, it is called with `training=False` (KerasModel) or after `model.eval()` (TorchModel) which switch off the dropouts.  This means that the values of `results` calculated in each iteration of the loop are identical.

The MultitaskRegressor model used in the uncertainty tutorial is not affected by this issue though.

I can try and submit a PR to address this issue if people agree?'

Title: b'peastman'
Body:
b"The models that support uncertainty don't rely on the `training` flag for dropout.  Instead they use an input argument to turn it on or off.  For example, in MultitaskRegressor:

https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/bf23ed30d5399d655ea828e5a45d97327271d9d6/deepchem/models/fcnet.py#L310-L311

When you call `predict_uncertainty()`, TorchModel passes `mode='uncertainty'` to the default generator.  The implementation of it for MultitaskRegressor enables the dropout flag in that case:

https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/bf23ed30d5399d655ea828e5a45d97327271d9d6/deepchem/models/fcnet.py#L384-L387"

Title: b'jc32173'
Body:
b'That works for the MultitaskRegressor, so this issue does not affect that model.

However, I thought the GraphConv and DAG KerasModels are also meant to support uncertainty prediction?  Both models have an `uncertainty` argument and have a variance output type,

e.g. for GraphConv:

https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/bf23ed30d5399d655ea828e5a45d97327271d9d6/deepchem/models/graph_models.py#L973-L974

and for DAG:

https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/bf23ed30d5399d655ea828e5a45d97327271d9d6/deepchem/models/graph_models.py#L688-L692

As far as I can see there is no input argument to turn dropouts on during `predict_uncertainty()` for these models?'

Title: b'Different y values between the AWS CSV file and different splitting methods'
Body:
b'##  Bug

The y values in the datasets loaded from deepchem vs the y values in the AWS CSV files are different. 
They also differ depending on how the data is loaded (index split or random split) with random split generating different values each time.

## To Reproduce

Lipophilicity benchmark as an example.

```
import deepchem as dc
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from rdkit import Chem

seed = 123
np.random.seed(seed)

# Get the index splitting of the Lipo benchmark from Deepchem &  merge them
_, datasets, _ = dc.molnet.load_lipo(featurizer='raw', splitter='index', seed=seed, reload=False)
all_dataset = dc.data.DiskDataset.merge(datasets)
d_index = {'smiles': [Chem.MolToSmiles(i) for i in all_dataset.X], 'exp_index': all_dataset.y.flatten()}
df_index = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(d_index)
df_index.set_index('smiles', inplace=True)

# Same as above but use random splitting
_, datasets_rand, _ = dc.molnet.load_lipo(featurizer='raw', splitter='random', seed=seed, reload=False)
all_dataset_rand = dc.data.DiskDataset.merge(datasets_rand)
d_rand = {'smiles': [Chem.MolToSmiles(i) for i in all_dataset_rand.X], 'exp_rand': all_dataset_rand.y.flatten()}
df_rand = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(d_rand)
df_rand.set_index('smiles', inplace=True)

# Load direct from the csv
# download "https://deepchemdata.s3-us-west-1.amazonaws.com/datasets/Lipophilicity.csv"
df_csv = pd.read_csv('Lipophilicity.csv)
df_csv.set_index('smiles', inplace=True)

# merge them on their index (set to the SMILES strings) to compare the y values
# call dropna to only get those where the SMILES string match (could also regenerate the strings with RDKit for df_csv)
merged = pd.concat((df_csv, df_index, df_rand), axis=1)
merged[['exp', 'exp_index', 'exp_rand']].dropna().head()
```
Run 1:
![lipo_numbers](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6068434/198555147-81f04c7b-6e8d-4dda-a35f-563cae77a56c.png)

Run 2:
![lipo_numbers_2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6068434/198556609-75f7bdfe-facf-4464-8b8b-6d1500e27acb.png)

Using 'random' splitting generates slightly different results each time, compare 'exp_rand' in Run 1 and Run 2. 

The y values from the AWS hosted csv ('exp' column) are wildly different to the ones loaded from the deepchem module.

## Environment

* OS: MacOS 12.6 (M1 Macbook)
* Python version: 3.9.13 (M1 native)
* DeepChem version: 2.6.1 (M1 native, conda-forge)'

Body:
b'Probably, the random seed is not enough to make the thing completely reproducible.
If the values are normalized once and for all for the whole dataset, it might stabilize the values.
I suspect there is a problem in deepchem: rather than passing a seed around, you should pass a properly seeded RNG.
Then, any code needing randomness should use that RNG.

b'Hello,

It would be nice to have a non programmatic way to limit the max number
of cores used at run-time.
For example:
```
DEEPCHEM_MAX_THREADS=1 ./my_deepchem_script.py
```
Thanks,
F.
'

Title: b'peastman'
Body: b"In the current version of TensorFlow, the way you limit the number of cores is with the ConfigProto you pass to the Session's constructor.  See https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38187808/how-can-i-run-tensorflow-on-one-single-core for details.  TensorGraph has a `configproto` argument you can use to specify that.\r\n\r\nThis is going to change in TensorFlow 2, though, since Sessions won't exist anymore.  I've been looking through the docs, but I haven't figured out what the new way of setting it will be."

Title: b'gusty1g'
Body:
b"Sorry for the delayed response but thanks for bringing this up @ismorphism @bananenpampe. The error can be reproduced in the following snippet:
```
import deepchem as dc

import numpy as np
X = np.random.randn(1000, 10)
n_classes, n_tasks = 3, 2
y = np.random.randint(low=0, high=n_classes, size=(1000, n_tasks))

train_dataset = dc.data.NumpyDataset(X=X[0:800], y=y[0:800])
valid_dataset = dc.data.NumpyDataset(X=X[800:], y=y[800:])

metric = dc.metrics.Metric(dc.metrics.prc_auc_score)
validation = dc.models.ValidationCallback(valid_dataset, interval=10, metrics=[metric])

model = dc.models.MultitaskClassifier(n_tasks=n_tasks, n_features=10, n_classes=3)

model.fit(train_dataset, callbacks=[validation])
```

As @ismorphism shared, the default value gets passed and the code doesn't care. The broader issue here is the code assumes at many places `n_classes` to be 2 rather than None when it is not specified, for example in dc.metric.Metric.compute_metric, dc.model.evaluate.Evaluator.compute_model_performance etc.

For this specific scenario, there are couple of solutions:
1. Make `n_classes` as an additional arg in initialization of `ValidationCallback`, thereby `n_classes` could be passed to evaluation method.
2. Callbacks are called in dc.models.KerasModel/TorchModel. During the call, we can pass the `n_classes` argument inferred from the model, like adding these two lines in `keras_model.py` and `torch_models.py`
```
if hasattr(self, 'n_classes'):
  n_classes = self.n_classes
else:
  n_classes = None
for c in callbacks:
  c(self, current_step, n_classes)
```
3. Update dc.model.Model.evaluate to have `n_classes` as an optional argument instead of the default 2 and check whether the n_classes attribute is present in the model. If present, pass it to evaluator or pass None in case if the attribute is not present.

I think having None as default value for n_classes will be better because it will be explicit to the users and the default value of 2 makes sense only in case of classification models, not in regression models."

Title: b'Data compression DiskDataset'
Body:
b'##  Feature

DiskDataset is very helpful when dealing with large datasets that do not fit in memory. However, the stored data, specifically high-dimensional X NumPy arrays of each shard, take up a lot of disk space when screening very large libraries. It would be great to support the compressed `.npz` format using `numpy.savez_compressed` and make it the default format instead of the vanilla `numpy.save`

Links:
https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.savez_compressed.html
https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/2.6.1/deepchem/data/datasets.py#L1331
https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/2.6.1/deepchem/utils/data_utils.py#L469



'

Title: b'peastman'
Body: b"Assuming the compression doesn't hurt loading speed, this seems like a good idea.  If it does make loading slower, it should probably be an option but not the default."

Title: b'ashtawy'
Body: b"@peastman agreed regarding saving/loading speed and exposing compression as an optional feature in DiskDataset. However, I haven't noticed a significant difference between `npy` and `npz` files when saving/loading several datasets in the past. Time spent saving the featurized dataset is usually a fraction of the featurization time, so it is effectively negligible. One can profile the loading time to decide whether the npz option should be the default or not.\r\n"

Title: b'rbharath'
Body: b'CC @arunppsg who has been also thinking of ways to lower storage requirements for large `DiskDataset` objects.\r\n\r\n@ashtawy Nice suggestion! Do you have a sense of how big the space difference is for .npz files instead of .npy files?'

Title: b'ashtawy'
Body: b'Generally, the saving is a function of the data (entropy) since compression algorithms take advantage of data repetition to reduce the number of bits required to save the data. For drug-discovery applications, the saving can be more than 30X cheaper when dealing with binary data (molecular fingerprints are binary most of the time and they can be binarized/bucketed if they are continues to make model training more stable). This can literally save us 30X in $ when storing our data on AWS S3 or EFS. '

When deepchem is imported, we import molnet loader functions and there is `load_perovskite` which uses CGCNNFeaturizer as a default featurizer. Title: b'peastman'

tasks, datasets, transformers = dc.molnet.load_tox21(featurizer='GraphConv')

import deepchem as dc

metric = [dc.metrics.Metric(dc.metrics.roc_auc_score)]

Title: b'[RFC] Long CI runs'
Body: b'DeepChem CI runs take a long time and it slows down developement time. One of the factors for long CI runs is running unit tests on multiple python versions - for example, unit test on torch CI runs on python 3.7, 3.8, 3.9.\r\n\r\nSince unit tests runs same test on different environments, as long as it works in one version, it should also work in another version. I suggest we can run unit test on only one main version (say py 3.8). But we should run build tests on all versions.'

Title: b'peastman'
Body: b"Running tests on multiple versions is important, because changes to Python do sometimes break things.  But it's generally ok to test just two versions: the oldest and newest ones you want to support.  If it works on those, you can be pretty confident it will also work on versions between them."

Title: b'NamedTemporaryFile function under windows'
Body:
b"Hi,
I tried to run the MUV inotebook and got some errors with 
> [Errno 13] Permission denied 

when trying to read or write from temp file.

I found the error online with the solution
[http://zachmoshe.com/2017/04/03/pickling-keras-models.html](url)
And adding delete=False to the 4 instances of NamedTemporaryFile in the file deepchem\hyper\__init__.py from
`tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile()` to
`tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False)`
solved the problem.

However I don't know if this option will break the module to run on Linux, and also if this is desirable (default is to delete the file)
See [https://docs.python.org/3.5/library/tempfile.html#tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile](url) for the doc on NamedTemporaryFile and the windows/Linux behaviour  "

Title: b'Converting large disk dataset to csv'
Body:
b"When there is a requirement to convert disk dataset to csv, currently we can only do it be converting it to a dataframe and then to a csv. But a drawback of this approach is that DiskDatasets which are large in size generate dataframes which don't fit in memory.  Having a method which can convert a large diskdataset to csv without consuming memory will be useful.

I would like to suggest an improvement to `class Dataset` by adding a `to_csv` method. This method can then use `itershards` to write data to a csv file.
"

Title: b'peastman'
Body: b'`itershards()` is a method of DiskDataset.  If we want to put the method in the parent Dataset class (which seems like the best place for it, so you can write out any dataset), we can use `itersamples()`.'

Title: b'GraphData class not working for single atom mols'
Body:
b"##  Bug

`GraphData` class checks if the `edge_index` contains the invalid node number, using the condition `np.max(edge_index) >= len(node_features)`. In case of single atom mols, `edge_index` in an empty array of `shape = (2, 0)` and np.max() method raises error for empty array : `Error: zero-size array to reduction operation maximum which has no identity`.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behaviour:

code to check the error:
```
    num_nodes, num_node_features = 1, 32
    num_edges = 0
    node_features = np.random.random_sample((num_nodes, num_node_features))
    edge_index = np.empty((2, 0), dtype=int)
    graph = GraphData(node_features=node_features, edge_index=edge_index)
    assert graph.num_nodes == num_nodes
    assert graph.num_edges == num_edges
    assert str(graph) == 'GraphData(node_features=[1, 32], edge_index=[2, 0], edge_features=None)'
```
error  message: 
`py::TestGraph::test_graph_data_single_atom_mol Failed with Error: zero-size array to reduction operation maximum which has no identity`

## Expected behaviour

No error should have raised and  `str(graph)` should return `'GraphData(node_features=[1, 32], edge_index=[2, 0], edge_features=None)'`

## Environment

* OS: Ubuntu 20.04.3 LTS
* Python version: Python 3.8.8
* DeepChem version: 2.6.1
* RDKit version (optional):
* TensorFlow version (optional):
* PyTorch version (optional):
* Any other relevant information: NA

## Additional context

This is how Deepchem generally computes edge index:
```
# construct edge (bond) index
    src, dest = [], []
    for bond in datapoint.GetBonds():
      # add edge list considering a directed graph
      start, end = bond.GetBeginAtomIdx(), bond.GetEndAtomIdx()
      src += [start, end]
      dest += [end, start]
```"

Title: b'Logging training of TorchModels to WandB'
Body:
b'##  Questions & Help

I am trying to log model training of a TorchModel to WandB and have some ideas for improvements:

1. The ValidationCallback is very useful to log metrics for both the validation and the training dataset. Right now the data is logged to wandb using
`data = {'eval/' + k: v for k, v in scores.items()}` and integers can be appended to the key if there are several datasets.
In my opinion, it would be better to have a parameter to control the prefix of the dictionary key when using the ValidationCallback for different datasets. This is what it currently looks like:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/107413352/174792587-45905ccd-5f96-477d-a1e3-186f9b88fa97.png)


2. The comments in ValidationCallback are all about Keras models only, but the code seems to work well for PyTorch models. Are there any known issues with PyTorch models or are the comments just outdated?

3. Afaik, the current solutions to get the validation loss are quite hacky (see #1040) and require looping manually over the epochs.  Instead, we could add this functionality to the ValidationCallback (on demand).


I have seen that there are bigger plans to improve the logger integration in general (see #2580), but it looks as if they have been "work in progress" for quite some time...
So I wanted to know your opinions on these small improvements before trying to tackle them and creating a PR.
'

Title: b'rbharath'
Body:
b"1. Good idea here. I like the concept of a new prefix
2. This is an oversight in the docs. I believe `TorchModel` should have full support for wandb
3. Adding validation loss calculation to `ValidationCallback` would be very nice! There have been a couple other request for this feature

I believe #2580 is stalled at present (@kshen3778 please correct me if I'm wrong here). Please feel free to go ahead and take on these small improvements! I think they would add value to the community"

Title: b'j-frie'
Body:
b'Thanks for the quick feedback :-)

What is the recommended way to check whether the model that calls the `ValidationCallback` is a `TorchModel` or a `KerasModel`?

The loss calculation is slightly different for the models, but I cannot simply check, if model is an instance of `TorchModel`, because if `torch`is not installed, one cannot import `TorchModel` (and similar for `KerasModel`, if tensorflow is not installed).

The solution I came up with is a bit long, so I was wondering if there is a better way to do it:
```
tf_installed = False
torch_installed = False
try:
  from deepchem.models.keras_model import KerasModel
  tf_installed = True
except ModuleNotFoundError:
  pass
try:
  from deepchem.models.torch_models import TorchModel
  import torch
  torch_installed = True
except ModuleNotFoundError:
  pass
```
The loss calculation within `ValidationCallback` looks like this:
  ```
def _calculate_loss(self, model):
    if torch_installed and isinstance(model, TorchModel):
      outputs = torch.from_numpy(model.predict(self.dataset))
      labels = torch.from_numpy(self.dataset.y)
      weights = torch.from_numpy(self.dataset.w)
      return model._loss_fn([outputs], [labels], [weights]).item()

    elif tf_installed and isinstance(model, KerasModel):
      outputs = model.predict(self.dataset)
      labels = self.dataset.y
      weights = self.dataset.w
      return float(model._loss_fn([outputs], [labels], [weights]))
```'

Title: b'peastman'
Body: b"The way you've written it, you require all outputs, labels, and weights for the entire dataset to be held in memory at once.  That's ok for small datasets, but it won't be practical for larger ones.  I wonder if we can come up with a solution that's both clean and robust.  For example, we could add an `evaluate_loss()` function to Model.  Or can we somehow create a Metric that evaluates a model's loss function?"

Title: b'j-frie'
Body:
b'That's a good point!

I have now wrapped the loss function (`model._loss_fn`) within the `Model` class to make it usable as a metric function in `Metric`.
```
  def loss_as_metric(self, y_true, y_predicted, sample_weight) -> float:
    """Wrapper to make loss function of Model usable as Metric.

    dc.metrics.Metric expects the metric function to have the args:
    y_true, y_pred, sample_weight
    loss function uses [outputs], [labels], [weights]"""
    loss =  float(self._loss_fn([y_predicted], [y_true], [sample_weight]).numpy())
    return loss
```

In `ValidationCallback` one can then use the existing way to evaluate metrics:
```
loss_metric = Metric(model.loss_as_metric, name='vc_loss', mode='regression')
model.evaluate(self.dataset, [loss_metric], transformers=[], use_sample_weights=True)
```

However, for classification problems, this is a bit tricky, and I need some help:

Some losses like `SoftmaxCrossEntropyLoss` take logits as inputs, but others like `BinaryCrossEntropy` take the output directly. 
How does the model know whether to use logits or outputs for the loss calculation? Is that hard-coded in every single model and we would have to add `evaluate_loss()` to `Model` and override it in all classification models depending on the loss function that is used?'

Title: b'Some of Dataset object methods does not work with ConvMol featurizer'
Body:
b"Let me begin with a simple code snippet:
```python
import deepchem as dc
tasks, datasets, transformers = dc.molnet.load_delaney(featurizer='GraphConv')
train_dataset, valid_dataset, test_dataset = datasets
train_dataset.make_tf_dataset()
```
It fails with the following error:
```python
In [9]: train_dataset.make_tf_dataset()
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
AttributeError                            Traceback (most recent call last)
<ipython-input-9-7aba8715e4d6> in <module>
----> 1 train_dataset.make_tf_dataset()

~\Documents\GitHub\deepchem\deepchem\data\datasets.py in make_tf_dataset(self, batch_size, epochs, deterministic, pad_batches)
    525     # Retrieve the first sample so we can determine the dtypes.
    526     X, y, w, ids = next(self.itersamples())
--> 527     dtypes = (tf.as_dtype(X.dtype), tf.as_dtype(y.dtype), tf.as_dtype(w.dtype))
    528     shapes = (tf.TensorShape([None] + list(X.shape)),
    529               tf.TensorShape([None] + list(y.shape)),

AttributeError: 'ConvMol' object has no attribute 'dtype'
```

The reason for this failure is `ConvMol` object has no `dtype` attribute.
https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/355954b37d333fc3e2c3b3e28d103297eb642769/deepchem/data/datasets.py#L526-L527

There are other `Dataset` object methods that do not work with the `ConvMol` object. For example, the following snippet will cause an error:
```python
import deepchem as dc
tasks, datasets, transformers = dc.molnet.load_delaney(featurizer='GraphConv')
train_dataset, valid_dataset, test_dataset = datasets
train_dataset.get_statistics()
```

The following error occurs:

```python
In [8]: train_dataset.get_statistics()
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TypeError                                 Traceback (most recent call last)
<ipython-input-8-ce6b52a0ebd8> in <module>
----> 1 train_dataset.get_statistics()

~\Documents\GitHub\deepchem\deepchem\data\datasets.py in get_statistics(self, X_stats, y_stats)
    464       n += 1
    465       if X_stats:
--> 466         dx = X - X_means
    467         X_means += dx / n
    468         X_m2 += dx * (X - X_means)
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'ConvMol' and 'float'
```
This error happens because the `ConvMol` object has no `__add__` method, so we can not use addition or subtraction on this object.

https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/355954b37d333fc3e2c3b3e28d103297eb642769/deepchem/data/datasets.py#L463-L468

I have not searched for all the `Dataset` methods exhaustively, but I suspect there are other methods that can not work with the `ConvMol` object or other faturizers that don't produce an array. 


"

Title: b'On argument types to deepchem layers'
Body:
b'DeepChem has pytorch, tensorflow and jax layers. Different layers use different array data types for computation (ex: pytorch - torch.Tensor, jax - jnp.ndarray).

A broad question here is what should be the input argument to `forward`/`call` methods of layers? We can either have it the input corresponding to layers backend (ex: torch.Tensor in case of pytorch) or we can have it more generally as `numpy.ndarray` for all kind of layers and internally convert it to a form corresponding to the backend.

Having it as numpy.ndarray as input data type has two advantages: the data objects represent data as numpy arrays and it can be uniform across layers, so users need not worry about data type will training models. But calling, say `torch.from_numpy()` for every forward call is going to be computationally expensive.

Another idea is to use a helper function which can convert the data type of data objects into the corresponding backends data type of the model/layers which is going to be used.
'

Title: b'peastman'
Body: b"The goal of the [Python array API standard](https://data-apis.org/array-api/latest/) is to let you write a single piece of code that works with any of these types.  Numpy 1.22 added preliminary support for it.  PyTorch is currently working on adding support.  I'm not sure what the status of Jax support is.\r\n\r\nClearly we can't rely on it quite yet.  But hopefully we can soon write all our layers to use the standard API and have them automatically work with any type of input."

Title: b'rbharath'
Body: b"Thinking about this, I propose for now we just standardize on all DeepChem layers using torch tensors. In the future torch tensors should eventually become compliant with the Python Array API standard so I think we should be reasonably future proof this way. (Jax tensors are another option, but I think Jax isn't stable on Windows yet and torch is more mature)"

Title: b'peastman'
Body: b"A corollary to that is that as far as possible, we should manipulate those tensors using the methods and arguments of the API standard.  PyTorch has been gradually tweaking its API to support the standard.  It isn't all the way there yet, but the closer we can get the code now, the less we'll have to change later."

Title: b'Cannot install on ARM Macs'
Body:
b"I recently got an ARM based Mac.  In trying to install DeepChem from source, I discovered that the install_deepchem_conda.sh script fails.  The first problem is that DGL is only available for x86 Macs, not ARM ones.  (See the list of packages for [pip](https://pypi.org/project/dgl/) and [conda](https://anaconda.org/dglteam/dgl)).  That's a serious problem, since we use DGL for a lot of models.  We should contact the developers to find out whether they plan to add support.

The second problem is that pip doesn't have TensorFlow for ARM Macs either.  Conda does, though.  The `tensorflow` and `tensorflow-probability` packages are both available from conda-forge, but `tensorflow-addons` isn't.  The `esri` channel has it, but only for Linux and Windows.  The `isuruf` channel has it for Mac, but it's an older version: 11.2 rather than 13.0.

The final error comes from jax:

> ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement jaxlib>=0.1.37 (from optax==0.0.8->-r /Users/peastman/workspace/deepchem/condaenv.cpr7qbjx.requirements.txt (line 13)) (from versions: none)

Title: b'Support for COLL Dataset'
Body:
b'COLL Dataset is a dataset of molecular dynamic simulations of molecular collisions. The dataset contains energies and forces of a random snapshot of 140, 000 collision simulations of molecules. It was introduced in the [Klicpera et al, 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.14115) (see sec 3 on details about the dataset).

The authors state that unlike established molecular benchmark sets like QM9, which consist of equilibrium or near-equilibrium configurations, the structures in COLL can be highly distorted. In particular, stretched bonds and angles as well as open-shell electronic structures will be prevalent.

It will be nice to add COLL dataset to moleculenet suite since benchmarking in COLL dataset will be a added value to DeepChem as it is contains more challenging molecular structures.'

Title: b'Improve Documentation for ValidationCallback to Assist with Hyperparameter Tuning'
Body:
b"##  Feature

I took a closer look at ValidationCallback in deepchem/models/callbacks.py and I don't think any more code needs to be written. There is already an attribute named self._best_score and an argument named save_on_minimum which allows choosing minimize or maximize. 

I have a few ideas: 1) Add a function to ValidationCallback called GetBestScore() or something. It may honestly not be necessary as like I said, self._best_score is already there. 2) Edit the dc.hyper.GridHyperparamOpt tuner to use the best validation score. I think it currently evaluates the FINAL model on the validation set instead of the BEST model but please correct me if I'm wrong. Then document this change clearly so others who wish to create a new hyperparameter optimizer will have an example to follow.

I think as a follow up, actual early stopping where the model saves the best model and stops if it doesn't improve after n steps would be a really nice feature to have, although I'm sure it'd be very complicated to implement across so many models. 

## Motivation

Allowing users to access the best validation score for the purpose of early stopping is very important for hyperparameter optimization. This feature is already there but the question is how do we make it easier to use/develop with. 

## Additional context"

    model.save_checkpoint(model_dir=self.save_dir)
```

Suggested solution:
```
if self._best_score is None or score < self._best_score:
    model.save_checkpoint(model_dir=self.save_dir, save_name_base="some_str")
```

### Pytorch changes

```

```

```

[Keras/TF Changes location](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/b26a60148521b49286ce6d5e619f3d82cda77611/deepchem/models/keras_model.py#L1045)

```

```
manager = tf.train.CheckpointManager(self._checkpoint, model_dir,
                                         max_checkpoints_to_keep, checkpoint_name=f'{save_base}')
```

## Motivation

Currently, the model checkpoints but does not include the option to use a filename. Using a common filename for validation callback would facilitate easy grepping of multiple models. Additionally, it appears as if pytorch and tf models are inconsistent in naming, and this will allow for better cross-model consistency.

DeepChem currently uses `dc.feat.graph_data.GraphData` for handling graphs. I think it will be more apt for `GraphData` to be under the `dc.data`, thereby making them a fundamental data type supported by DeepChem.

### Motivation
- Graph based data types seems to be a very common kind of data type used in scientific applications.
- We can add more support for handling graphs and performing operations on them - like saving, loading, converting it to other formats etc

For doing the transition, we can probably begin with createing `dc.data.GraphDataset` class like `dc.data.NumpyDataset` which can take in node features and edge features - just like `dc.feat.graph_data.GraphData` but under `dc.data`. Next, we can add a depreciation note and update code in repository to use dc.data.GraphDataset. Later on, we can add more support on handling (like saving, retrieving) graphs.

Some features which will be nice to see (feel free to add yours):
- Conversion of pytorch-geometric, networkx and other graph forms to dc.data.GraphDataset and vice-versa
- Utilities to compute graph properties like centrality measures, etc'

def create_reset_model_callback(interval):

b'Steps to reproduce:

```
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
featurizer = dc.feat.WeaveFeaturizer()
X = featurizer(["C", "CC"])
y = np.array([[1], [0]])
dataset = dc.data.NumpyDataset(X, y)

model = dc.models.WeaveModel(n_tasks=1, n_weave=2, fully_connected_layer_sizes=[100], mode="regression", nb_epoch = 1,
                             activation=tf.nn.sigmoid, final_conv_activation_fn=tf.nn.sigmoid, compress_post_gaussian_expansion=True, 
                             gaussian_expand=False)
loss = model.fit(dataset)

model.predict(dataset)
```

The above code raises the following error:
```
ValueError: Exception encountered when calling layer "weave_gather_23" (type WeaveGather).

in user code:

    File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/dist-packages/deepchem/models/layers.py", line 3086, in call  *
        output_molecules = tf.matmul(output_molecules, self.W) + self.b

    ValueError: Dimensions must be equal, but are 128 and 1408 for '{{node weave_gather_23/MatMul}} = MatMul[T=DT_FLOAT, transpose_a=false, transpose_b=false](weave_gather_23/SegmentSum, weave_gather_23/MatMul/ReadVariableOp)' with input shapes: [?,128], [1408,128].
```

This is probably due to the use of `gaussian_expand` and `compress_post_gaussian_expansion` options. It occurs only when they are (True, False).'

Title: b'On testing model reloads'
Body:
b"In DeepChem's test for model [reloads](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/deepchem/models/tests/test_reload.py), some tests have the following workflow:

1. Generate a dummy dataset
2. Create a model
3. Train the model
4. Eval model on train data and assert scores
5. Reload the model
6. Check whether predictions match or not
7. Evaluate the reloaded model and assert scores

I have some questions on the above workflow:
- We are evaluating the model and asserting the scores as part of [model tests](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/tree/master/deepchem/models/tests). So, can we eliminate steps 4 and 7?
- The test for model reload should test whether a reloaded model has same predictions as original model or not. If I am not wrong here, we need not train the model in reload tests. We can drop step 3. This will simplify make model reload tests simpler as well reduce time taken for CI completion. Because, when we are increasing the number of models, training a model in each CI run is going to take time. Training them again when testing reload can take a even longer time.

Apart from these, some of the model tests are flaky. The amount of flaky tests can be reduced."

Title: b'Creating a Model Contribution Guide for DeepChem'
Body:
b'Contributing a model to DeepChem requires a good bit of work. Adding a guide that walks new developers through the process of contributing a model starting from an open source implementation not in DeepChem would be very valuable. Here is what the guide should cover

0. Motivation: Why do you want to add this model to DeepChem? Usually, this is to build a robust standard implementation that will be maintained for the long run and usable at scale.
1. Data Loading: How does the original repo load data? How can you convert this to use DeepChemic style? Recall DeepChem uses `DataLoader` objects to load data from disk. Is there a `DataLoader` for this datatype? If not, should we add one?
2. Featurization: How does the original code featurize loaded data? Recall featurization is the process of transforming raw data into a form suitable for machine learning. DeepChem uses `Featurizer` objects to do this. Can we reuse an existing featurizer? Do we need to add a new featurizer?
3. Model Conversion: DeepChem has standard methods for porting Keras/PyTorch/Jax models into DeepChem. Walk through taking model code in one of these frameworks and wrapping it in DeepChem. Often the biggest challenge is that DeepChem uses `Dataset` objects as its standard tool to pass around data. `Dataset` objects will need to be unwrapped/wrapped in the model wrapper
4. Metrics: Are there any nonstandard metrics needed to benchmark the external model? Should we add them?
5. Datasets: Is it worth adding any of the datasets used by the new model to MoleculeNet?

Ideally, the person writing this guide should have experience contributing a model to DeepChem! The guide should be added to the docs in the `docs/` folder or optionally may be written up as a colab notebook.
'

b'##  Feature

The numpy requirement >=1.21 is too strict and causes a lot of dependency issues with other packages.

Title: b'Tutorial Request: Using Docker Images to Run Old DeepChem Versions'
Body: b"A common issue DeepChem users have is that they wrote code for an old version of DeepChem which no longer runs on new DeepChem. We've taken a lot of effort to start enforcing strong backwards compatibility in recent releases but some changes are out of our control (for example, TensorFlow 1 to TensorFlow 2 broke our checkpointing). It's also often very challenging to get old versions of python packages running since you need to ensure that all versions of dependencies are set correctly.\r\n\r\nLuckily we've maintained docker images for DeepChem for a number of years now. It would be very useful for the community to have a guide on how to use these docker images to run old DeepChem code. A good guide would give a basic introduction to docker, an explanation of how the deepchem docker image works, and a guide for how to run an old deepchem script using the docker image. In addition, the tutorial should explain how to copy data into and out of the docker container."

Title: b'use of str() in temp filenames can break due to length.'
Body:
b"##  Bug
`load_dataset` in `molnet_loader.py` attempts to create a temporary directory using `str(self.featurizer)`, which falls back to the `__str__` implementation in `base_classes.py`. This builds the representation from concatenating all the non-list, non-path values of the class. This can easily be long enough to generate a filename with is over the maximum the OS supports.


## To Reproduce
````{python}
import deepchem as dc
import string
def build_char_dict():
    cti = {}
    for i, x in enumerate(string.printable):
        cti[x] = i
    cti['<unk>'] = max(cti.values()) + 1
    cti['<pad>'] = max(cti.values()) + 1
    return cti
char_to_idx_dict=build_char_dict()
featurizer = dc.feat.SmilesToSeq(char_to_idx=char_to_idx_dict)
tasks, datasets, transformers = dc.molnet.load_qm7(
    featurizer = featurizer,
    splitter='random')
````
## Expected behavior
load_qm7 works and does not throw an exception

## Environment

* OS: windows 10
* Python version: 3.7
* DeepChem version: 2.5
* RDKit version (optional): 
* TensorFlow version (optional): 2.7
* PyTorch version (optional):
* Any other relevant information:

## Additional context
As a minor aside, use of unsanitised string values in filenames is not a great idea security wise, this could probably be exploited to escape a jupyter shell - this should probably be handled using the `tempfile` module instead.
"

Title: b'Consolidating deepchem installation using .yml files'
Body:
b'Currently, there are multiple .yml files which are to be merged for DeepChem installation. They are also at two places - few in the [root](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/) directory and couple of others in [requirements](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/tree/master/requirements) directory. This is causing some confusion on which .yml files are used for setup and installation of dependencie in different environments.

Ideally, all installation .yml files should go into requirements directory. We should consolidate the required installation files and remove the redundant ones. Also, corresponding changes has to be made in installation of deepchem in github workflows and docs.

Listing the .yml files and their ideal use cases:

Common - These yml files should contain the libraries which DeepChem uses internally (like numpy, pandas etc). They should not contain the backend frameworks for deep learning. 
- [requirements/env_common.yml](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/requirements/env_common.yml)
- [env.common.yml](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/env.common.yml)

Test - the libraries here are installed only during testing purposes and they are not required otherwise (like end use).
- [env.test.yml](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/env.test.yml)

The below three contain the installation procedure for backends in different backend environments.
Jax related:
- [requirements/jax/env_jax.cpu.yml](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/requirements/jax/env_jax.cpu.yml)
- [requirements/jax/env_jax.gpu.yml](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/requirements/jax/env_jax.gpu.yml)
- [requirements/jax/env_jax.yml](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/requirements/jax/env_jax.yml) - probably this can be removed as it is similar to common .yml files.

Torch related - contains torch related dependencies:
- [requirements/torch/env_torch.cpu.yml](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/requirements/torch/env_torch.cpu.yml)
- [requirements/torch/env_torch.gpu.yml](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/requirements/torch/env_torch.gpu.yml)
- [requirements/torch/env_torch.yml](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/requirements/torch/env_torch.yml)  - probably this can be removed as it is similar to common .yml files.

Tensorflow related:
- [requirements/tensorflow/env_tensorflow.yml](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/requirements/tensorflow/env_tensorflow.yml) - This should be updated to include tensorflow related dependencies and remove libraries which are part of common .yml files.

Core - with the use of seperate torch, tensorflow and jax installation procedures, I think these files are not required:
- [env.cpu.mac.yml](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/env.cpu.mac.yml)
- [env.cpu.yml](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/env.cpu.yml)
- [env.gpu.yml](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/env.gpu.yml)

Feel free to chip in your ideas. Thanks!

CC @rbharath 
'

- Do we really need seperate .yml files for different environment? - less files, low maintenance overhead.

Title: b'gusty1g'
Body:
b"The error is occurs in sklearn version 0.24 onwards. DeepChem's models inherit `sklearn.base.BaseEstimator`. For the children classes of `BaseEstimator`, it requires that the parameters in `__init__` to be retrieved as an instance attribute of the same name which raises the error.

There are two possible fixes for this:

1. Create instance attributes of all arguments in `__init__` with the same name. I feel this is a not so nice solution as it will create instance attributes which are not going to be used. A fix like this was done in this [PR](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/pull/2671/files)
2. We can remove `Model` class from being an  `sklearn.base.BaseEstimator`. The `BaseEstimator` was introduced in this [PR](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/pull/544) to try out different parameters for hyper-parameter optimization via the library [osprey](https://github.com/msmbuilder/osprey). Two points to note here is that DeepChem is currently not using `osprey` since it has its own support for hyper-parameter optimization and we are also not using `get_params()` and `set_params()` provided by `BaseEstimator`.

I prefer the latter approach but open to any suggestions/thoughts."

b'I'm reaching the conclusion that notebook is just a mess.  I'm trying to figure out what it's doing and why, but with only partial success.  Here's what I've figured out so far.

It begins by downloading two CSV files and loading them into memory.  It confusingly assigns them to variables called `dataset` and `crystal_dataset`, even though they're actually Pandas DataFrames, not Datasets.  There's no explanation for any of this code, including any description of what's in those files it's loading.

It plots a bunch of molecules from both files, but there's no explanation of why it does this or what we're supposed to learn from them other than the one vague sentence, "Note the complex ring structures and polar structures."

It now uses a UserCSVLoader to create actual Datasets from those files.  Just to be extra confusing, it assigns them to the same variables it previously used for the DataFrames, `dataset` and `crystal_dataset`.  It specifies that the "Class" column should be loaded as the labels, but gives no information about what's contained in that column.

It splits it into train, validation, and test datasets.  It comments without explanation that the test set is really a validation set and the validation set is really a test set.  I have no idea what it's talking about.  It also applies normalization and clipping transformers.  The text says these are being applied to the pIC50 values, which is false: as noted above, the Dataset used the "Class" column, *not* the "pIC50" column.

It fits RandomForestClassifiers and MultitaskClassifiers to the training set (again emphasizing that the labels are classes, not continuous values, so the transformers made no sense) and computes the AUC on the various datasets. Anyway, as it currently exists this notebook is not a tutorial.  It's just a bunch of code, some of it nonfunctional, with very little explanation of what it's doing or why.     self.logits = layers.Reshape((n_tasks, 2))
    self.softmax = layers.Softmax()

  def call(self, inputs):
    a = self.gc1(inputs)
    b = self.batch_norm1(a)
    c = self.gp1([b] + inputs[1:])

    d = self.gc2([c] + inputs[1:])
    e = self.batch_norm1(d)
    f = self.gp2([e] + inputs[1:])

    g = self.dense1(f)
    h = self.batch_norm3(g)
    i = self.readout([h] + inputs[1:])

    j = self.logits(self.dense2(i))
    return self.softmax(j)

Body:
b'##  Bug

<!-- A clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->
This bug arises when attempting to reshard a `DiskDataset` created using `CSVLoader`. I believe the reason this happens is because the `create_dataset()` method of  the `DataLoader` class  sets y to `None` in the `shard_generator()` method,  if the labels column is empty ([for reference](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/deepchem/data/data_loader.py#L219)). As a result, when the dataset is resharded, the call to the `generator` method fails since it requires the length of the column. 


## To Reproduce
The dummy dataset I will use to illustrate the problem looks something like [this: ](https://github.com/Suzukazole/deepchem/blob/usptotok/deepchem/data/tests/reaction_smiles.csv)
```
reactions
CCS(=O)(=O)Cl.OCCBr>CCN(CC)CC.CCOCC>CCS(=O)(=O)OCCBr
CC(C)CS(=O)(=O)Cl.OCCCl>CCN(CC)CC.CCOCC>CC(C)CS(=O)(=O)OCCCl
O=[N+]([O-])c1cccc2cnc(Cl)cc12>CC(=O)O.O.[Fe].[Na+].[OH-]>Nc1cccc2cnc(Cl)cc12
Cc1cc2c([N+](=O)[O-])cccc2c[n+]1[O-].O=P(Cl)(Cl)Cl>>Cc1cc2c([N+](=O)[O-])cccc2c(Cl)n1
```

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
```
# file_path is path to above dataset file

>>> featurizer = dc.feat.DummyFeaturizer()
>>> loader = dc.data.CSVLoader(tasks=[], feature_field="reactions", featurizer=featurizer)
>>> dataset = loader.create_dataset(file_path)
>>> dataset.reshard(shard_size=10)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/deepchem/deepchem/data/datasets.py", line 1477, in reshard
    generator(), data_dir=reshard_dir, tasks=self.tasks)
  File "/deepchem/deepchem/data/datasets.py", line 1204, in create_dataset
    for shard_num, (X, y, w, ids) in enumerate(shard_generator):
  File "/deepchem/deepchem/data/datasets.py", line 1461, in generator
    y = np.reshape(y, (len(y),) + y_shape[1:])
TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()
```
<!-- If you have a code sample, error messages, stack traces, please provide it here as well. -->

## Expected behavior
It should reshard the above dataset to a `shard_size` of 10.

<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->

## Environment

* OS: Ubuntu
* Python version: 3.7.0
* DeepChem version: 2.6.0dev(this [branch](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/pull/2641))

## Additional context
Above error came up while coming up with a fix for the splitter bug, which happens due to a similar reason as well.

Title: b'Difference between sklearn OneHotEnconder and DeepChem OneHotFeaturizer'
Body:
b'##  Questions & Help

<!-- A clear and concise description of the question. -->

The use of some sklearn functionalities into deepchem will help solve problems like handling large dataset with memory expensive datasets and featurization process such as the sparse_matrix_one_hot_enconder https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/issues/2778#issue-1065978426 
However there is a difference in both tools in the handle of unknown characters. For example, in the deepchem oneHotFeaturizer. 
```
  >>> one_hot_encode(3, [0, 1, 2], include_unknown_set=True)
  [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]
```
While the OneHotEncoder of Sklearn has a handle_unknown  {error, ignore}, default=error

> handle_unknown{error, ignore}, default=error
>
>   Whether to raise an error or ignore if an unknown categorical feature is present during transform (default is to raise). When this 
Parameter is set to ignore and an unknown category is encountered during transform, the resulting one-hot encoded columns for this 
feature will be all zeros. In the inverse transform, an unknown category will be denoted as None.

I do not know if this difference could cause some problems in later implementations

'

Title: b'Rename ComplexNeighborListFragmentAtomicCoordinates to AtomicConvFeaturizer and add predict_embedding'
Body:
b'There are currently two featurizers associated with atomic convolutions:

- `ComplexNeighborListFragmentAtomicCoordinates`: This featurizer computes the coordinates needed for `AtomicConvModel`
- `AtomicConvFeaturizer`: This featurizer was introduced in https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/pull/1476. It computes a "neural fingerprint" which embeds co-crystal structures as a vector. To clarify, it trains an internal `AtomicConvModel`, then extracts fingerprints by invoking this trained model on new complexes it's supposed to featurize.

This state of affairs is quite confusing to beginners who naturally expect that `AtomicConvFeaturizer` is the featurization for `AtomicConvModel`. I propose therefore that we make the following changes:

- Rename `ComplexNeighborListFragmentAtomicCoordinates` to `AtomicConvFeaturizer`. Keep `ComplexNeighborListFragmentAtomicCoordinates` as a deprecated wrapper for the next release.
- Remove the current `AtomicConvFeaturizer`. Instead, add a `predict_embedding()` function to `AtomicConvModel` that retrieves the co-crystal fingerprints.

What do folks think about this proposal?

CC @peastman @vsomnath  '

## Expected behavior
The contained values should be the same between the two files, and the file opened via `load_qm8` should contain the data from `LR-TDPBE0/def2TZVP`

Title: b'Upgrading autodock vina to 1.2.2'
Body:
b'One of the pose generators used by DeepChem is Autodock Vina. Recently, the latest version of vina 1.2.2 was released. With this release, the invocation calls - the parameters and arguments changed. The Vina team have also released a python API for docking.

Should we migrate to the newer version?

An issue with the existing version is that the download link for v1.1.2 has changes and from our end, we need to update the download links for using `VinaPoseGenerator` in DeepChem. (see #2737)

A challenge with the newer version is that, from my understanding, it uses `PDBQT` files instead of `PDB` files as input for AutoDock Vina (see [here](https://autodock-vina.readthedocs.io/en/latest/docking_basic.html#preparing-the-receptor)). Hence, we need to [create](https://ccsb.scripps.edu/adfr/how-to-create-a-pdbqt-for-my-receptor/) pdbqt receptor for using autodock vina. I am not sure whether this can be circumvented (did minimal tests and using pdb files as input failed). 
'

Title: b'Error in intializing VinaPoseGenerator'
Body:
b"##  Bug

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Install deepchem latest version in colab `pip install --pre deepchem`
2. Run the following code sample:
```
import deepchem as dc
vpg = dc.dock.VinaPoseGenerator()
```

The above raises a`SSLCertVerificationError` but it is expected to initialize `vpg`.

There are two points regarding this:
- The download location of autodock vina executables was updated from the side of Vina team. Previously, DeepChem referenced them from [here](http://vina.scripps.edu/download/autodock_vina_1_1_2_mac_64bit.tar.gz) but now it is referenced from [here](https://vina.scripps.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/55/2020/12/autodock_vina_1_1_2_mac_64bit.tar.gz)
- There is some problem in the server side which is causing `SSLCertVerificationError`, probably an expired SSL Certificate.

Some possible fixes:
- Move the executables to DeepChem's infrastructure
- Upgrade to the latest version of Autodock vina - 1.2.2"

Title: b'Tutorial Request: In-depth Model Contribution Guide'
Body:
b"DeepChem now has first class support for TensorFlow/PyTorch/Jax models. We should now be able to support basically all the models developed by ML researchers. However, the process of contributing a new model to DeepChem is still not well documented. We should have an in-depth guide that a researcher who's interested in contributing a model to DeepChem can follow . This tutorial should have the following components:

- How to convert an arbitrary Torch `nn.module` to work with `TorchModel` with discussion of Gotchas.
- How to convert an arbitrary kears model to work with `KerasModel`.
- How to convert an arbitrary jax model to work with `JaxModel`.

We have some documentation for this already, but I'm looking for a more in-depth guide that talks through common edge cases. I've gotten some feedback that it can be tricky to use `TorchModel/KerasModel` if you're new to DeepChem and its conventions. 

The goal for the tutorial is that we have a guide we can share with leading research labs in the space to encourage their students/researchers to contributed models to DeepChem that they've developed"

Title: b'Grid Hyperparameter logdir behavior not documented'

Title: b'rbharath'
Body:
b"The randomness is training definitely makes models behave differently on different runs. One good solution to something like this is to use ensemble median voting.

1. Train K models on your source dataset for K large (10 or 15). 
2. Make predictions as the median of the K model predictions

I've been meaning for some time to build some DeepChem tooling to facilitate this process, but for now, you should be able to do this manually. The median voting will stabilize predictions and will probably boost your model accuracy too. Saving/restoring is now fixed for GCNNs (on the latest nightly build) so you should be good to go with saving/restoring models!"

Title: b'Consider (enforcing) commit signing or 2FA'

b"Commit signing ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/free-pro-team@latest/github/authenticating-to-github/signing-commits), [benefits](https://softwareengineering.stackexchange.com/questions/212192/what-are-the-advantages-and-disadvantages-of-cryptographically-signing-commits-a)) was mentioned in the meeting today, so I figured I'd make an issue for it.

It's possible to [enforce commit signing](https://docs.github.com/en/free-pro-team@latest/github/administering-a-repository/enabling-required-commit-signing) in PRs, but in my experience it's an undue burden on first-time contributors. FWIW, [nodejs, rejected the idea](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/15457). I think if we want serious repo security, we should probably do what they do and [require collaborators use 2FA on GitHub](https://docs.github.com/en/free-pro-team@latest/github/setting-up-and-managing-organizations-and-teams/requiring-two-factor-authentication-in-your-organization).
"

Title: b'alat-rights'
Body:
b'Here's my proposal for a sort of maximal reasonable security approach in this regard:

People who do code review/merge commits keep some sort of signed, distributed notebook of secure (read: not SHA-1!) hashes of merged commits once in a while. This makes release signing very easy. 

The contents can be released in quarterly signed "canaries" [Qubes style](https://github.com/QubesOS/qubes-secpack/blob/master/canaries/canary-024-2020.txt).

2FA would, of course, be a plus. But not security critical in this case.

--------------

Here's the problem with 2FA: it relies on infrastructure security. The recent Twitter hack (wherein the attacker was purportedly able to directly access the CPanel and thus attain control of any account) shows that this is an incredibly flawed approach. 

While enforcing 2FA is a low-risk, low-cost approach (and a lower-cost, higher-reward policy change that can go hand-in-hand with this would be requiring code reviewers to use effective (read: non-SMS and preferably Yubikey-based) forms of 2FA), we should probably have a proper discussion about the Deepchem threat model at some point. I suppose that Deepchem may be considered security-critical in certain academic settings? But I think a serious discussion of threat modelling would certainly be in order before we implement any changes as drastic code-signing. 

--------------

Summary:
- Code signing likely less effective than signed commit-logging by reviewers
- 2FA is good and cool.
- Requiring "good" (non-SMS) 2FA for reviewers makes sense.
- Better threat modelling of Deepchem is a reasonable goal over the next few months. '

Title: b'[Question]  When should I pass "Transformers" to the method `model.predict_on_batch` or `model.predict`?'
Body:
b'##  Questions & Help

Hi, Thank you for sharing your great code. I just started to use DeepChem. 

I am following the [tutorial](https://github.com/deepchem/deepchem/blob/master/examples/tutorials/01_The_Basic_Tools_of_the_Deep_Life_Sciences.ipynb). I have a few questions about `model.predict_on_batch` and `transformers`:


Q1) According to the [documentation](https://deepchem.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_reference/models.html#deepchem.models.KerasModel.predict_on_batch), `predict_on_batch` has an argument called `transformers`. However, in the following line of the code, `transformers` is not passed. My question is when I should pass `transformers` to the method `model.predict_on_batch` or `model.predict`.

`solubilities = model.predict_on_batch(test_dataset.X[:10])
`


Q2) According to the [documentation](https://deepchem.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_reference/models.html#deepchem.models.KerasModel.predict_on_batch), `transformers` is:

`Transformers that the input data has been transformed by. The output is passed through these transformers to undo the transformations.`

I have misunderstanding about `transformers`.

Q2-1) In the above definition, what does `input data` mean? Is it X data (features or input to the model) or Y data (model output)?

Q2-2) Why do we need to undo transformation on output?

From my previous experience in machine learning, I used to apply Normalization or Standard Scaling on X (input to the model or features). I would like to ask the reason of `output is passed through these transformers to undo the transformations`.


Q3) What is the different between `model.predict_on_batch` or `model.predict`? If I want to get prediction for the whole test dataset, should I use:

`solubilities = model.predict(test_dataset.X)
`

Thank you for your time to read my questions. 


'

Title: b'gusty1g'
Body:
b'Hey, sorry for a very late response. From the best of my understanding,

On 1)
Transformer has to be used on test dataset when the train dataset is transformed using a transformer for training. In such cases, `transformers` parameters can be used to specify the same transformation used on the training dataset to the test dataset. When a dataset loaded from `dc.molnet` submodule is used, `transformers` argument need not be passed during prediction because the train dataset and test datasets are already transformed (transformer argument is passed during loading as an argument to `dc.molnet.load_X()`).

On 2-1) `input data` refers to train dataset. The second line - `The output is passed through these transformers to undo the transformations` is not clear for me also. Tagging @rbharath for this.

On 3) 
`model.predict_on_batch` predicts on a sample of data. It can be used like `model.predict_on_batch(test_dataset.X)` or it can also be used to predict on a set of samples like `model.predict_on_batch(test_dataset.X[:10])`.  
`model.predict` is used to predict on the entire dataset. It takes `deepchem.data.datasets.Dataset` as parameter. Example usage: `model.predict(test_dataset)`.

'

Title: b'mohammad-saber'
Body:
b'Thank you for your help. 

I guess the meaning of `The output is passed through these transformers to undo the transformations` is :

We want to get model output in original scale (without transformation) for the purpose of plotting or comparing with `y_true` in original scale. '

Title: b'gusty1g'
Body: b'Yes, when the model is making predictions, the predictions will be transformed outputs. Hence, we are undoing the transformation applied on the predictions to get the original value.\r\n\r\nA bit of example: The true y is of range 0-100, suppose we transform it to a scale of 0-1 during training, the model output will also be in the scale of 0-1. Hence, we undo the transformation in the output by passing it to the transformers to get the predicted  output in the original scale. For generating loss function, we use the scaled values since it gives more numerical stability.'
